mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and leads to lower S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces wage growth and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which adversely affects earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a simultaneous monetary tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases risk premia and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 5-year moving average by more than 10% in a single month signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST jumps above its 5-year MA by more than 10% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates a statistical artifact or data reclassification event, which historically has coincided with market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises while UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) below 1% for four consecutive quarters signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand for goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS annualized growth < 1% for 4 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when RSAFS annualized growth is below 1% for four consecutive quarters.
